title: env-log-level
request: Can we add support for a LANGFUSE_LOG_LEVEL env var so I can set the logger level (e.g. INFO) without using the debug flag? It should respect the existing LANGFUSE_DEBUG flag too.
reference_diff:
--- a/langfuse/logger.py
+++ b/langfuse/logger.py
@@ -12,10 +12,24 @@
 """
 
 import logging
+import os
 
 # Create the main Langfuse logger
 langfuse_logger = logging.getLogger("langfuse")
-langfuse_logger.setLevel(logging.WARNING)
+# Determine logger level from environment variables
+if os.getenv("LANGFUSE_DEBUG", "").lower() in ("true", "1"):
+    langfuse_logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
+else:
+    log_level_str = os.getenv("LANGFUSE_LOG_LEVEL")
+    if log_level_str:
+        # Convert string level name to numeric level, default to WARNING if invalid
+        level = getattr(logging, log_level_str.upper(), None)
+        if isinstance(level, int):
+            langfuse_logger.setLevel(level)
+        else:
+            langfuse_logger.setLevel(logging.WARNING)
+    else:
+        langfuse_logger.setLevel(logging.WARNING)
 
 # Configure httpx logger to reduce noise from HTTP requests
 httpx_logger = logging.getLogger("httpx")

+++ b/tests/unit/test_logger_env_level.py
@@ -0,0 +1,15 @@
+import os
+import importlib
+import logging
+
+def test_log_level_via_env():
+    os.environ["LANGFUSE_LOG_LEVEL"] = "INFO"
+    try:
+        # Reload the logger module to pick up the new env var
+        import langfuse.logger as logger
+        importlib.reload(logger)
+        from langfuse import Langfuse
+        Langfuse()
+        assert logger.langfuse_logger.level == logging.INFO
+    finally:
+        os.environ.pop("LANGFUSE_LOG_LEVEL")
